title: PyTorch pt2 archive validation: scan data.pkl with pickletools for user-registered safe globals instead of changing torch's process-wide safe_globals registry
answers: Why do concurrent torch.load(weights_only=True) calls fail while an MLflow pt2 model is being loaded?
Why does a pt2 model containing a class I registered with add_safe_globals get rejected on load?
Where does MLflow handle torch safe_globals during pt2 archive validation?
body:
Path: mlflow/pytorch/__init__.py:_validate_pt2_archive_is_pickle_free calls _user_registered_safe_globals (reads torch.serialization.get_safe_globals()) and _pickle_globals (a pickletools.genops scan of each record's data.pkl) for every record it validates.
Rule: When validating untrusted torch pickle data, do not add to or clear torch.serialization safe globals process-wide. Instead, statically scan the data.pkl opcodes (GLOBAL and STACK_GLOBAL, resolved from preceding string operands) and reject any record that references a user-registered global, or whose stream cannot be parsed or resolved (fail closed). Then run torch.load(weights_only=True) unmodified on records that pass.
Symptom: An earlier validator approach cleared the safe_globals registry during validation. On torch 2.8, a concurrent torch.load(weights_only=True) of a checkpoint that used a registered metadata class succeeded before and after validation but raised UnpicklingError while validation ran.
Constraints: Only the pt2 validator uses this scan. Registered globals still work for ordinary torch.load calls outside pt2 validation. Built-in torch allowlist entries are not rejected by this scan. Tests: test_load_pt2_model_validation_ignores_ambient_safe_globals and test_load_pt2_model_validation_does_not_disturb_concurrent_weights_only_loads in tests/pytorch/test_pytorch_model_export.py.
applies: Any MLflow code that runs torch.load(weights_only=True) or torch.serialization safe-globals checks on attacker-controllable pickle data, mainly the pytorch pt2 validator.
says: Loading a saved model crashes other concurrent checkpoint loading jobs in the service.
Exported model validation rejects files containing custom classes registered as safe.
Simultaneous model loading tasks fail with deserialization errors while archive security checks run.
Prevent archive verification checks from clearing registered safe types across concurrent tasks.
search: For PyTorch pt2 archive validation, MLflow statically scans data.pkl opcodes with pickletools.genops to detect user-registered safe globals rather than modifying torch.serialization safe globals process-wide. In mlflow/pytorch/__init__.py:_validate_pt2_archive_is_pickle_free, calls to _user_registered_safe_globals and _pickle_globals inspect GLOBAL and STACK_GLOBAL opcodes, rejecting records referencing user-registered globals or unparseable streams. Records that pass are loaded unmodified with torch.load(weights_only=True), avoiding UnpicklingError during concurrent loads on PyTorch 2.8. This scan applies only to the pt2 validator, leaving registered globals intact for normal torch.load calls outside pt2 validation and allowing built-in Torch allowlist entries.
